EXCEEDS_INITIAL.note: Their answer is larger than the amount they started with, so more reactant was consumed than existed. Impossible whatever the algebra did.
EXCEEDS_INITIAL.ask: Compare your number with the amount you started with. Can more react away than was there?

ORDER_OF_OPERATIONS.note: Their number is what x^2/a0 - x gives when the denominator is not bracketed: (x^2/a0) - x, a different equation.
ORDER_OF_OPERATIONS.ask: Say out loud what is on the bottom of your fraction. How would you have to write it so a calculator reads the same thing?

COEFFICIENT_NOT_SQUARED.note: They used x where the expression needs the coefficient: (2x) squared, not x squared.
COEFFICIENT_NOT_SQUARED.ask: How many product molecules does one reaction event make, and where does that number go in the expression?

INITIAL_IN_K.note: They put the initial concentrations into the equilibrium expression. The products start at zero, so K came out zero.
INITIAL_IN_K.ask: Which row of your table belongs in the equilibrium expression, and why that one?

EQ_COEFFICIENT_NOT_SQUARED.note: Their expression holds only with 2x squared read as 2·x², not (2x)².
EQ_COEFFICIENT_NOT_SQUARED.ask: What is being squared in the numerator: x, or the whole concentration of the product?

EQ_ORDER_OF_OPERATIONS.note: Their expression holds only when read as (x²/a0) − x: the denominator was not bracketed.
EQ_ORDER_OF_OPERATIONS.ask: Which terms are in the denominator of your expression, and does your line say so?

openers.title: V2 opener 1
openers.question: A sealed clear soda bottle sits quiet, but a pressure sensor reveals gas molecules are escaping and redissolving at identical speeds without any net change in bubble size. What are the dissolved and gaseous carbon dioxide particles doing at the liquid boundary to preserve this motionless standoff?

openers.title: V2 opener 2
openers.question: A sealed jar of smelling salts maintains a sharp sting, yet a gas meter logs solid particles decomposing while vapor particles constantly recombine into solid. What are the solid and vapor particles doing during collisions that keeps their respective total amounts completely fixed?

openers.title: V2 opener 3
openers.question: A sealed glass tube holds reddish-brown gas at a steady color tint, while an optical sensor shows dimeric pairs continually splitting and single molecules pairing up. What are the brown and clear gas particles doing during encounters to leave the visible tint perfectly stable?

openers.title: V2 opener 4
openers.question: A bottle of salad vinegar tastes sour, but an ionization scanner shows only a tiny fraction of acid molecules ever yield ions while ions rapidly recombine. What are the intact acid molecules and separated ions doing in the solvent that prevents total ionization?

openers.title: V2 opener 5
openers.question: A half-filled vintage perfume bottle never runs dry, as an ultrasonic sensor tracks liquid molecules continuously evaporating while vapor molecules crash back into the pool. What are the surface molecules doing on both sides of the interface to lock the liquid volume in place?

openers.title: V2 opener 6
openers.question: A cloudy fish tank water sample stops depositing white mineral crust, while an ion counter logs calcium ions precipitating as solid crystals simultaneously dissolve. What are the dissolved ions and solid mineral particles doing at the glass edge to halt further crust growth?

expression_set.ask: Write the equilibrium expression with the equilibrium row of your table substituted in, on one line, with brackets around every numerator and denominator.

value_found.return_ask: What did the notebook show you about going from x to the answer?
